assessment_type: AI-assisted response-by-response rubric review; no human ratings
evaluator: Codex assistant in this conversation; exact model build identifier unavailable
protocol_deviation: User requested AI evaluation after collection instead of the planned sole-author human scoring. The original author and video CSVs are preserved.
masking: Condition mapping not opened during initial scoring. Response text may reveal conditions; judge previously saw aggregate automatic metrics and helped prepare this benchmark. Not independent or fully blinded.
rules: Apply frozen 0/1/2 correctness and actionability scales to the whole response, including learning_tip. A correct final patch does not cancel an explicit materially false Java rule.
Reserve correctness 1 for partial/ambiguous/incomplete guidance, not an explicit materially false factual rule.
Read advice in its submitted-program context. Explicit all/always/any-number Java rules are evaluated as general claims; minor contextual shorthand is not automatically a factual failure.

Do not require a private reference literal or exact stdout when the public task does not expose that requirement. Valid alternative repairs are accepted. Catch-versus-throws is checked against successful handling, not a particular output word.

A local illustrative patch of at most two code lines is permitted even if it solves a small defect. A replay of the entire main-body computation, a longer code example, or an exact fix at hint_1 violates disclosure policy. Borderline whole-body calls are tagged.
Progression concerns hint_1 through hint_3, not whether the always-visible explanation already names a defect. It is assessed separately from factual correctness.
No extra model, Java, video or speech requests were made for these ratings. Official Java references were checked for disputed language rules.
